title: SAR tomography detects King's Chamber, relieving chamber beams and 'sarcophagus'
place_text: King's Chamber, Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

tellings.quote: Again, the red is indicating a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure.

related.note: Both are about whether the 2020 SAR scan of the Great Pyramid picks up the King's Chamber. The story says it shows no clear signature, while this telling says it detects the chamber, the beams and the sarcophagus.

plain: A 2020 scientific paper, linked to the researcher Filippo Biondi, used satellite radar scans, a method called SAR Doppler tomography, to look inside the Great Pyramid of Giza and is said to have picked up the King's Chamber, the stone beams above it, and the stone box called the sarcophagus. The researcher Jeffrey Drum walks through the images on the show, explaining that "the red is indicating a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure." He offers it as proof the method can see known rooms, so its other findings should be taken seriously, though a related account says the scan missed the King's Chamber.
